title: Why These 5 Stocks Are Crashing (But I'm Buying More)
creator: Asymmetric Investing
summary: Travis Holm of Asymmetric Investing presents five high-growth companies — each with a compound annual growth rate over 30% over the past three years — that have crashed hard and, in his view, are now phenomenal prices. Axon, which he has owned for over a decade, is down ~64% from its 2025 peak despite a 10-year revenue CAGR of 30%, long-term law-enforcement platform contracts, and expansion into drones (P/E ~36, P/FCF ~44). Zeta Global, a recent portfolio addition, is compounding revenue at almost 40% since mid-2024 with operating margin now positive and ~$260m of free cash flow over the past year; its 2028 targets ($2.3bn revenue, $371m FCF) look likely a year early, and Athena OS moves it into business intelligence. Sezzle, the buy-now-pay-later company, has grown revenue at over 50% CAGR since end-2022 (5-year CAGR 41%, ~$4.8bn enterprise value, forward P/E ~21) but he has never owned it and would only buy at a better price in 2027, flagging short-term default risk. Hims & Hers is down to ~$14 — below its Novo Nordisk lawsuit low — despite 64% revenue compounding over almost five years and ~50% growth expected in the second half of 2026, trading at just 1.4x sales. TransMedics, the organ-transplant logistics company, has a 91.5% five-year revenue CAGR and is expanding into Europe. Calls: AXON BUY (first tracked), ZETA BUY (reiterated), SEZL CONDITIONAL_BUY (first tracked), HIMS BUY (flip from HOLD), TMDX BUY (first tracked). He also promotes a 25%-off Fiscal AI deal. Note: the caption garbles Sezzle as 'Sle'/'Szle' and TransMedics as 'Transmetics'.

calls.thesis: First tracked. Axon is 'one of the best companies in the world' and he has owned shares for more than a decade. Down ~64% from its 2025 peak, but a 10-year compound annual revenue growth rate of 30%, with long-term platform contracts from law-enforcement agencies; P/E ~36 and P/FCF ~44 for a still very high-growth business expanding into drones.
calls.base: The platform keeps compounding revenue at ~30% and the drawdown proves to be the opportunity.
calls.bull: Drones and the platform expansion re-accelerate growth and the multiple expands.
calls.bear: Heavy SG&A/R&D spending keeps operating profit suppressed.

calls.video_title: Why These 5 Stocks Are Crashing (But I'm Buying More)
calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY (last BUY 13 Oct). Zeta is in the Asymmetric portfolio and 'the kind of company that's going to be a huge winner for investors over the next decade'. Revenue CAGR almost 40% since mid-2024, operating margin now positive, free cash flow ~$260M over the past 12 months; its 2028 targets ($2.3B revenue, $371M FCF, $573M adjusted EBITDA) look likely to be hit a year early in 2027, and Athena OS expands it from marketing into business intelligence.
calls.base: 2028 targets are hit in 2027 and the stock trades at ~20x FCF.
calls.bull: Athena OS 10x-es the business over the next decade.

calls.thesis: First tracked. Sezzle (caption garbles the name as 'Sle'/'Szle'; identified from the buy-now-pay-later description) is a 'phenomenal' comeback: ~$4.8B enterprise value, revenue CAGR over 50% since end-2022, 5-year CAGR 41%, forward P/E ~21, P/FCF ~12. He has never owned shares and it is not in the portfolio, but 'if we get a little bit better price in 2027, wouldn't mind owning a few shares'. Conditioned on a better price. Risk flagged: it takes on short-term default risk like a bank.
calls.base: A better price in 2027 lets him start a position.
calls.bull: Growth and operating leverage keep compounding and the multiple expands.
calls.bear: Consumer defaults rise and hit the bottom line.

calls.thesis: FLIP: last stance HOLD (after the Q3 disappointment, when he stopped adding). 'I stay bullish on him and hers' — shares now ~$14, below even the level at the Novo Nordisk lawsuit bottom. Revenue has compounded 64% over almost 5 years, with ~50% growth expected in H2 2026 partly from acquisitions, and the enterprise value is just $4B at 1.4x sales. calls.base: The platform keeps compounding and the 1.4x sales multiple re-rates.
calls.bull: Peptides and the early-2027 weight-loss platform launch re-accelerate growth.
calls.bear: Margin compression and branded-product pricing pressure persist.
